hypothesis: Adding a reflexion editor to the RAG draft should improve coverage and question quality by dropping already-given or low-value questions and filling in decision-critical unknowns (budget/timeline/goal etc.) that the initial draft missed.
technique: Two-stage pipeline: stage 1 is the exp003 RAG-generate draft; stage 2 is a second FM call (auditor) given the draft plus a fixed universal decision-critical checklist (budget/who-for/timeline/scale/location/current-state/goal), instructed to delete given/low-value/compound questions and insert the highest-value missing unknown while keeping strong questions verbatim.
result: Scored 0.315 on dev-10 (0 wins / 1 tie / 9 losses vs Sonnet), down −0.005 from the exp003 best of 0.320; coverage stayed at 3 while nonRedundancy also held at 3, confirming the hypothesis was falsified — the hard universal checklist caused the auditor to mechanically inject irrelevant dimensions (budget/timeline into tasks where they're noise) and introduced new redundancy, swapping one set of wrong slots for another. Discarded.

stages.text: Fetch nearest gold exemplars via RAG
Auditor: drop weak Qs, fill checklist gaps
